Saved files opened from the mirror: title tag '(PDF) DICTIONARY OF THE MOMI [=VERE] LANGUAGE..', the phrase 'three level tones in Momi, as well as a rising tone' occurs twice in the embedded text) and lines 202-209: '3.3 Tones / There are three level tones in Momi, as well as a rising tone. A possible minimal triplet is; / séé arrow / see month; moon / sèè cooking stones; hearth / However, the tone-marking in the existing dictionary inconsistent and is omitted in the present document.' A's quote is verbatim…
new_statements.relation_note: Three level tones + rising tone; no word-stress statement.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Momi (Vere Kaadam, Yadim dialect) is a tone language with three level tones (high, mid, low) plus a rising tone, illustrated by the triplet séé 'arrow' / see 'month, moon' / sèè 'cooking stones, hearth'; nothing is said about word stress or accent, and tone is not marked in the dictionary body.
new_statements.exceptions: none; author notes the 1988 tone-marking was inconsistent ('sketchy') and is omitted in this edition
new_statements.identity_note: Momi of Yadim (Yola/Fufore LGAs, west of the Vere Hills) = Glottolog dialect Momi Yadim [momi1241] of Vere Kaadam [vere1252]; same authors/data as the 1988 Yadim-dialect dictionary that Glottolog attaches to vere1252 (ref 98222). Not Mom Jango [momj1237] or Northern Alantika Vere [nort3260]. Access note: the PDF download at Academia.edu is login-walled, but the document's full front-matter text is embedded in the public page (and its Internet Archive copy), which is what was read and. Glottolog and our bibliography list only the 1988 version (our held 2004 web draft lacks this introduction). | Verre of the Vere Hills (Cholli/Soli dialect of Chappel's and Meek's informants, north of the hills; Yadim dialect of B&E; Gweri of the VLP) = Vere Kaadam [vere1252]. Ethnographic/art-historical monograph; the phonological remarks are explicitly second-hand (from Blench & Edwards 1988 and the 2013 VLP pamphlet) and by non-linguists.

new_statements.quote: In the VLP transcription, Verre has eight vowels, one more than in B&E, who do not see a need to distinguish between ɛ and e. We shall retain eight vowels where Chappel's informants distinguished them (a e ɛ ə i o ɔ u). Long and short vowels are contrasted, and there appear to be three level tones, though we are unable to represent them here, let alone the glides between tones. There are twenty-two or twenty-three consonants in the contemporary transcriptions.
new_statements.citation: Chappel, Tim, Richard Fardon & Klaus Piepel. 2021. Surviving Works: context in Verre arts. Vestiges: Traces of Record 7(1), special issue (ISSN 2058-1963). new_statements.identity_note: Momi = Vere/Verre of Adamawa State, Nigeria, the language of the Blench & Edwards Yadim-dialect dictionary = Glottolog dialect 'Momi Yadim' under vere1252 (not Mom Jango momj1237). NB: the phonology section (3.1-3.3) is near-verbatim the same text as the front matter of Blench & Edwards 2021 'Dictionary of the Momi [=Vere] language' already quoted by pass 1 (PRIOR work 1, dated 16 Aug 2021); this is a distinct document (noun-morphology paper, 28 July 2021) by the same author from the same data, so it corroborates but is not an independent source.
